articles.title: EU tech chief says bloc well equipped to fend off rogue AI risk
articles.summary: EU tech chief Henna Virkkunen told Reuters that EU rules setting guardrails on AI use are more than capable of tackling rogue agents, following recent incidents at OpenAI and Anthropic. The AI Act, which regulates use based on risk level, is seen as the world's strictest AI rules. The Commission sent requests for information to more than 30 AI companies in late August; such requests can lead to investigations and fines of up to 7 percent of global annual turnover.

articles.summary: A bipartisan House trio outlined a sweeping new artificial intelligence proposal that would require companies to adhere to minimum federal safety standards and disclose any lapses while clarifying where liability lies for foreseeable injuries tied to the technology. articles.title: US AI Chip Crackdown Shakes Supply Chains
articles.summary: The US Commerce Department announced stricter export controls on AI chips, explicitly targeting data centers serving Chinese firms to close a loophole in prior restrictions. Nvidia confirmed it would halt sales of its most advanced chips to China, while Alibaba revised its cloud growth outlook downward citing the curbs as a direct constraint.

articles.title: Oil gains on Iran war worries and short-covering ahead of Thanksgiving holiday
articles.summary: Oil gained late in trading as worries about possible renewed attacks in the US-Israeli war with Iran and holiday short-covering lifted prices.
